meta.title: Peregrine: Free Open-Source Download Manager for Windows, macOS & Linux
meta.description: Peregrine is a free, open-source download manager and IDM alternative. Up to 32 connections per file, resume that survives crashes, a browser extension, torrents and video. No ads, no tracking.
meta.ogTitle: The Digital Peregrine: a free download manager that never starts over
meta.ogDescription: A field guide entry for Peregrine: up to 32 connections per file, progress saved every second, browser extension, torrents and video. Free and open source.

nav.book: A Field Guide to Free Software

entry.title: The Digital Peregrine
entry.lead: The fastest download manager in its habitat. It splits its prey into up to 32 parts, chases them all at once, and never gives up its progress: not on a dropped Wi-Fi, a crash or a power cut.
entry.facts: Free · open source (GPL-3.0) · no ads · no account · no tracking
entry.plate: Plate 1. In a stoop. The arrow points at your file.

notes.title: Field notes
items: Habitat
Windows 10 and 11, macOS 12 and later. Seen on Linux at the command line.
Also nests in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi through an extension that hands over downloads with their cookies.
Diet
HTTP and HTTPS, FTP, torrents and magnet links, HLS and DASH streams, video sites.
Does not eat your data. It makes no network requests except the downloads you start.
Behaviour
When one connection finishes its part, it stoops on half of the slowest part that is left.
So no connection ever sits idle while one slow part drags the download out.
Memory
Writes its position to a crash-safe database every second.
Bytes go to a .peregrine.part file and get the real name only after they are verified.

lab.title: Observed in captivity
lab.body: Before every release, the engine is released into an enclosure with a test server built to misbehave. These behaviours were provoked on purpose, and this is how it reacted:
rows: The server cuts the connection halfway through.
Reconnects and continues from the last byte it wrote.
Notices, falls back to one connection, and does not corrupt the file.
The server sends no file size at all.
The server swaps the file between requests.
Sees the changed ETag and starts clean instead of stitching two files together.
Pauses and lets you paste a fresh link. Everything already downloaded is kept.
The server answers 503 to the first tries.
Retries with back-off, then carries on.
Keeps every connection busy, so the total stays as fast as the line allows.
lab.note: The enclosure is in the repository: internal/testsrv.

faq.title: Notes from observers
items: Is Peregrine really free?
Yes. It is open source under GPL-3.0. There is no paid version, no trial, no ads and no bundled offers.
Is it a good alternative to IDM?

It covers what most people use IDM for: many connections per file, resuming broken downloads and catching downloads from the browser. It is free and also runs on macOS. It is an early preview, so expect rough edges and please report them.
Why does Windows SmartScreen warn me?
The builds are not code-signed yet. Click More info, then Run anyway. You can check the file against SHA256SUMS.txt and the signed build provenance on GitHub.
Does it work on Linux?
On Linux, Peregrine is a command-line tool for x64 and ARM64. The desktop app is for Windows and macOS.
Does it collect any data?
No. No analytics and no telemetry. It only connects to the internet for the downloads you start. This website has no trackers either.
